_about: Website wording for each feature in help-features.json, written for managers and non-technical readers. Keys are the product's feature titles; each value is [title shown on the website, one plain sentence]. The build warns when a listed feature has no entry here, or an entry no longer matches a product feature.
Active projects: Every live project with its progress, team and timeline, so you can see at a glance which ones are on track.
Kanban and Scrum: Run each project as a simple task list, a visual board of cards, or in short planned rounds of work called sprints.
Project calendar: All open projects on one monthly calendar, by start date and deadline.
Create and configure a project: Name it, choose the team and departments, and decide how its work should flow.
Project join requests: People ask to join a project, and its leads approve or decline.
Closed projects: Finished projects stay on record and can be reopened if the work picks up again.
Postponed projects: Pause a project without losing anything, and pick it up again later.
Tasks: Find any task you are allowed to see, by person, project, status or date.
Create a task: Give a task an owner, a due date, a time estimate and any notes or files it needs.
Task details and sub-items: Everything about a task in one place
Comments, issues, improvements and follow-up actions live on the task, not in email threads.
Task timers: People press start when they begin a task, so their hours are recorded as they work.
Away time prompt: If a computer is left asleep while a timer runs, the person is asked what that time was when they come back.
Task workflow: Work moves from doing, to checking, to finished, signed off and delivered, so everyone knows where it stands.
Send a task reminder: Send a reminder, with a note if you like, by notification and email.
Send reminders to your team: Remind the whole team at once
Nudge several people to close overdue tasks, fill in timesheets, send weekly updates or check their leave. HYCROS suggests who is behind.
Progress reviews: Reviewers look at work at set points on the way, so problems show up early rather than at the deadline.
Unassigned tasks: Spot tasks nobody has picked up and give them to someone.
Completed and postponed tasks: A record of what was finished, delivered, put on hold or cancelled.
Follow-up tasks on complete: When a task is finished, the next one can be created straight away, so nothing falls between the cracks.
Bulk upload tasks: Bring in a list of tasks from an Excel sheet instead of typing them one by one.
Task lifecycles: Choose the steps a task goes through, such as a standard flow or one for HR and payroll work, to match how your organisation runs.
Scheduled tasks: Daily or weekly duties given to people on a rota with a time slot, following your working days.
Bug tracker: Errors from your own software are collected and turned into tasks for the team to fix.
Due Date Change Requests: Nobody moves a deadline quietly. Changes come to you with a reason, and you approve or decline.
Estimate Hours Change Requests: If a task needs more hours than planned, the person asks with a reason, and you decide.
Documentation verification: Required documents are reviewed before a task can be marked finished.
Completion acknowledgements: Accept finished work, accept it with a note, or send it back with feedback.
Assignment approvals: Approve the proof someone submitted for a checklist, or send it back with a note.
Pending approval reminders: Managers with decisions waiting get a reminder every two hours during the working week. Nothing is sent when nothing is waiting.
Leave and WFH approvals: Approve requests in a click, and cancel an approved one with a reason if plans change.
Overdue task edit requests: Changing a duty after its time has passed needs a manager's approval.
Tasks and timesheet approvals: Task and timesheet decisions waiting for you, together in one place.
Report dashboard: Your starting point for reports, including how much of each person's month is already booked.
Resource allocation: How much of each person's time is booked on each project, who is overloaded, and suggestions for moving work.
Capacity and quality: Compare planned work with the hours people really have, and see how often work is sent back to be redone.
Team insights and portfolio: Spot people and projects at risk, see how long work takes from start to finish, and how reliably the team delivers on time.
Estimate vs actual: Compare how long work was expected to take with how long it really took.
Due date & estimate change reasons: Every deadline and estimate change, with the reason given.
Daily report: Hours worked, meetings held and tasks touched, day by day.
Team live status: See who is working, in a meeting or away, without having to ask.
Team work overview: Charts of hours by person, project and task, with what each person has on their plate.
Member report: One person's hours by day, project and task, with averages.
Report builder: Pick what to see, filter it, add a chart and save it, without exporting to a spreadsheet.
Saved reports: Download a saved report as a PDF, or have it emailed on a schedule. Each person only sees the people they are allowed to see.
Project report: The status and progress of your projects in charts, by date, category or person.
Task report: How many tasks are open, finished or late, who owns them, and how they compare with their estimates.
Timesheet report: Hours for any period, as totals or in detail.
Meeting minutes report: Find past meetings and the decisions recorded in them.
Release notes: What was delivered, where and when.
Activity logs: Search everything that happened on a project or task, even ones that were deleted.
Timeline replay: Play back what your team worked on between two dates, like a recording, to see where the time went.
Task governance: Confirm that tasks follow your rules for documents, checklists and approvals.
Leave & attendance report: Leave, work from home and attendance for your team in one summary.
Points leaderboard: People earn points for finished work, shown on a friendly team leaderboard.
Team SWOT report: Read the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats recorded for the people you lead.
Billing, billable tasks and profitabilit: See billable work and a profit forecast, based on the rates you set.
Client 360: One view of a client's projects, tasks, time spent and follow-ups.
Client actions and quarterly performance: Track calls and emails to clients against targets, quarter by quarter.
Quarterly revenue and targets: Track revenue each quarter and compare it with your targets.
Video duration report: For teams that make videos: the length of each video, recorded automatically.
Timesheets: Time from task and meeting timers goes into the timesheet automatically.
Add or edit a timesheet: Team leads can add or fix time that was missed.
Meeting timers and minutes: Time the meeting, write down decisions, and turn action points into tasks with owners when it ends.
Start a team meeting: Start the meeting clock for everyone attending, in one go.
Leave requests: People see their balance and apply for leave in a few clicks.
Work from home: Ask to work from home, and cancel the request if plans change.
Attendance: Check-in and check-out times from your attendance machine or selfie app, in one place.
Team calendar: Leave, work from home, holidays and booked work for the whole team on one monthly calendar.
Team attendance: Your team's attendance, with the option to correct a record when there is a genuine reason.
Team leave balances: How much leave and work from home each person has earned, used and has left.
Weekly update: Each person shares their priorities, progress, blockers and what help they need.
Team weekly updates: See who has sent their weekly update, and read them all in one place.
Employee SWOT: Record each person's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (a SWOT), with a plan to improve.
Department docs: Your processes and reference documents, shared with the right department.
Assignments: People work through checklists given to them or their team, and attach proof when done.
Create assignments: Send a dated checklist to a person or a whole department, and change or remove it later.
Lead Management: Follow every enquiry from first contact to won or lost. Response time counts working hours only, so weekends do not count against you.
Lead access: Managers decide who in their department can see sales enquiries. Nobody has access by default.
Clients: One list of clients and who looks after each, linked to their projects.
Client access: Share a private link so a client can see how their project is going, without an account and without seeing anything else.
Home: A home page for each role
Everyone sees what needs their attention first. Staff see their day, managers see their team's delivery, and the head of the company sees the whole organisation.
My Tasks: Each person's own list of work, sorted by what is due, with a timer on every task.
Priority matrix: Tasks sorted into four boxes (do now, plan for later, hand to someone else, or drop) based on deadline and priority.
Team dashboard: Every teammate's tasks on one screen, so you can follow up without asking.
Recent activity: Who did what on the tasks and projects you look after, and when.
Notifications: Each person chooses which alerts reach them in the app, by email or in Microsoft Teams.
Sticky Notes: A private to-do list for each person.
My Profile: Each person sets their name, password, time zone and how they want to be notified.
Festival mascot: The HYCROS mascot dresses up for the public holidays where each person lives.
Help center: Search a guide to every feature, kept up to date with each release.
Contact support: Ask the HYCROS team for help, and follow the reply in the product and by email.
Get the apps: Use HYCROS in the browser, on Windows or on Android.
Wellness reminders: Gentle reminders to take breaks and drink water.
Cherry on top: Daily puzzles and quick team games such as drawing, trivia and word games.
Find a buddy: Meet colleagues who share your hobbies and interests.
Members and work overview: Add staff one by one or from a list, and see each person's work history.
Departments and job titles: Set up your organisation's structure the way it really is.
User groups: Group people from different departments and give the whole group access to a project.
Organisation settings: Your company name, logo, working days, time zone and look, and how soon an unattended screen signs out.
Modules: Use only what you need. A feature you switch off disappears for everyone.
Leave HR hub: Set holidays, leave balances and allowances, and settle leave when someone leaves the company.
Multi-task time allocation: Let people who juggle several jobs run more than one task timer at the same time.
Email, Teams, SSO, and eTimeOffice: Link HYCROS to your email, Microsoft Teams, company login and attendance machines. Support emails can become tasks automatically.
SCIM provisioning: When someone joins or leaves in your company directory (such as Microsoft's), their HYCROS account is created or switched off automatically.
Work on tasks from Claude: People can ask Claude, an AI assistant, about their tasks, projects and hours in everyday language, and update them if you allow it.
Subscription: See your plan, how many people used it this month and your invoices, and update your payment card.
Data export: Download your organisation's data (people, projects, tasks, timesheets, leave and more) as spreadsheet files whenever you need it.
